# Technical Requirements for "Virtual Machine RTOS shall work as expected" (ISO 26262 Context)

First, an important note: **the original functional requirement as stated is non-compliant with ISO 26262**. The phrase "shall work as expected" is ambiguous, unverifiable, and violates ISO 26262-8:2018 Clause 6 (requirements must be unambiguous, verifiable, atomic, and feasible). It needs decomposition into concrete, verifiable technical safety requirements (TSRs).

Below is how this would typically be refined into proper technical requirements.

---

## 1. Temporal/Timing Requirements

| ID | Technical Requirement |
|---|---|
| TR-1.1 | The RTOS scheduler shall guarantee deterministic task activation within ≤ X µs jitter for ASIL-classified tasks. |
| TR-1.2 | The RTOS shall enforce worst-case execution time (WCET) budgets per task and detect deadline overruns within one OS tick. |
| TR-1.3 | The hypervisor shall provide time partitioning so that no VM can consume more than its allocated CPU budget (temporal isolation per ISO 26262-6, Annex D / freedom from interference). |
| TR-1.4 | Context switch latency between safety-critical VMs shall not exceed X µs. |

## 2. Spatial / Memory Isolation (Freedom From Interference)

| ID | Technical Requirement |
|---|---|
| TR-2.1 | The hypervisor shall enforce memory isolation between guest VMs using MMU/MPU/IOMMU hardware mechanisms. |
| TR-2.2 | Access violations between VMs shall be detected and reported to the safety monitor within X ms. |
| TR-2.3 | Shared memory regions between VMs shall be access-controlled (read/write/execute attributes per partition). |

## 3. Communication Isolation

| ID | Technical Requirement |
|---|---|
| TR-3.1 | Inter-VM communication shall use authenticated, integrity-protected channels (e.g., CRC, sequence counters). |
| TR-3.2 | Communication bandwidth between VMs shall be bounded and policed by the hypervisor. |

## 4. Error Detection & Handling

| ID | Technical Requirement |
|---|---|
| TR-4.1 | The RTOS shall detect kernel stack overflow, illegal instruction, and divide-by-zero exceptions and transition to a defined safe state. |
| TR-4.2 | A program-flow monitoring mechanism (e.g., logical/temporal supervision per ISO 26262-6, Table 4) shall be implemented for ASIL B+ tasks. |
| TR-4.3 | The hypervisor shall implement a watchdog supervising each guest VM with a reaction time ≤ FTTI. |
| TR-4.4 | Detected faults shall trigger an entry into the Safe State within the Fault Tolerant Time Interval (FTTI). |

## 5. Startup, Configuration & Integrity

| ID | Technical Requirement |
|---|---|
| TR-5.1 | The RTOS/hypervisor shall perform integrity checks (e.g., CRC32 or signature) on its image at boot. |
| TR-5.2 | Configuration data (scheduling table, partition config) shall be validated before activation. |
| TR-5.3 | The startup sequence shall complete within the defined initialization time budget. |

## 6. Qualification / Confidence in Use

| ID | Technical Requirement |
|---|---|
| TR-6.1 | The RTOS shall be qualified as a Software Component per ISO 26262-8 Clause 12, or developed compliantly to the target ASIL. |
| TR-6.2 | A Safety Manual shall define the assumptions of use (AoU) and integration constraints for the RTOS/hypervisor. |
| TR-6.3 | Tool qualification (TCL) shall be performed for the build and configuration tools per ISO 26262-8 Clause 11. |

## 7. Diagnostics & Safety Mechanisms

| ID | Technical Requirement |
|---|---|
| TR-7.1 | The RTOS shall support runtime diagnostics consistent with the achieved diagnostic coverage required by the FMEDA. |
| TR-7.2 | All safety mechanisms shall be testable at startup and/or periodically during runtime. |

---

## Recommended Refinement of the Original Requirement

Replace *"VM RTOS shall work as expected"* with, for example:

> **"The Virtual Machine RTOS shall provide deterministic scheduling, spatial and temporal freedom from interference between partitions per ISO 26262-6 Annex D, and detect/react to violations within the Fault Tolerant Time Interval, with safety integrity equivalent to ASIL [X]."**

---

If you share the **ASIL level**, the **safety goal**, and the **hardware platform** (e.g., Hypervisor on ARMv8-A with EL2, multi-core SoC), I can tailor these TSRs more precisely (e.g., specific metric values, IOMMU usage, lockstep considerations).
